approachQuestion.prompt:
Complete Label Strip

A strip is represented by lowercase string `strip`. A non-empty lowercase string `request` lists required label occurrences: repeated letters require that many copies. Return the inclusive index pair [start,end] of the shortest contiguous strip segment containing every requested occurrence, with additional letters allowed. Break ties by the smaller start. Return [-1,-1] if none exists.

Limits and assumptions:
• 0 ≤ n = strip.length ≤ 200000; 1 ≤ m = request.length ≤ 200000.
• Letters are from a to z; each character has one directly indexable code. The input must remain unchanged.

Examples:
1. strip = "cabaa", request = "aa" → [3,4].
2. strip = "baca", request = "ac" → [1,2], preferred over [2,3].
3. strip = "abc", request = "dd" → [-1,-1].

Choose one approach.
constraints: Letters are from a to z; each character has one directly indexable code. The input must remain unchanged.

options.text: Count the requested copies in 26 slots. Expand right while tracking how many requested copies remain missing. Whenever none are missing, record the candidate and remove from the left until coverage breaks. Keep the earliest start on equal lengths.
options.feedback: Coverage depends on multiplicity, and removing leftmost labels finds the shortest cover ending at each right boundary. Extra copies do not count as missing.

options.text: Maintain the same counts and shrinking procedure, but copy every covering candidate substring before comparing its length and start.
options.feedback: The selected indices are correct for all inputs, but copying candidates is unnecessary when only their indices are returned.

options.text: Track only whether each distinct requested letter is present. Shrink whenever all these distinct letters appear.
options.feedback: For strip "ab" and request "aa", presence of a is insufficient: two copies are required and no answer exists.

options.text: Check only segments whose length equals request.length and return the first with matching counts.
options.feedback: With strip "axb" and request "ab", the shortest cover is [0,2]; intervening labels are allowed and can force a longer segment.

feedback.reason: Missing copies decrease only when an incoming letter fills a requested deficit.
details: Build 26 requested counts. Maintain window counts and a missing-copy total, updating it only when an added or removed letter changes the number of fulfilled requested copies. While the window covers the request, compare length and start, save only indices, and remove its leftmost character.

Missing copies decrease only when an incoming letter fills a requested deficit. An extra copy does not satisfy another required letter. Shrink while coverage remains complete and use the stated earliest-start tie rule when lengths match.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only “Shrink a covering multiset” as specified in the method reveal. Choose the tightest worst-case running-time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Use unit-cost random access and arithmetic on machine words large enough for every index and sum.
Input is read-only and excluded from auxiliary space. The scalar or index-pair output is excluded; no candidate segment is copied.
The implementation is iterative with a constant call stack. No hashing is used; fixed alphabet arrays, when present, are direct indexed.

options.text: O(n + m) time, O(1) auxiliary space
O(n + m) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(n² + m) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Build badge counts and scan strip boundaries with fixed-alphabet storage.
details: Building requested counts reads m characters. Each strip position enters once and leaves at most once, giving O(n + m) total time. Two 26-slot arrays and scalar state suffice. Missing-copy transitions preserve multiplicity; shrinking enumerates the shortest cover for each end and the explicit tie rule chooses the earliest start.
“O(nm) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The badge is counted once, not matched from scratch at every strip position; strip boundaries each advance at most n times.
“O(n + m) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Requested and window counts each have 26 slots, and best coverage stores indices rather than copied substrings.
“O(n² + m) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Repeated shrinking removes each strip character at most once; it does not rescan every candidate start.
